Understanding your dental condition is the first step to better oral health. Here we share clinical insights from our practice.

Dental Abscess

Dental Abscess — Why Timely Treatment Matters

A dental abscess occurs when a tooth becomes infected and can no longer be treated with simple fillings. Such a tooth will require root canal treatment or may need to be extracted.

Root canal treatment saves the tooth and restores it functionally, after which a crown is placed. If left untreated, the abscess can spread to adjacent teeth and surrounding areas, causing serious infections such as cellulitis — a life-threatening condition that can block the airway passage and create a medical emergency.

Timely intervention is essential to salvage the tooth and prevent further complications.
Root Canal Treatment Dental Crown Tooth Extraction

Composite Filling

Tooth-Coloured Composite Filling — Restoring Decayed Teeth Naturally

When a tooth develops a cavity, early intervention with a composite (tooth-coloured) filling is the most conservative and effective way to restore it. The decayed portion is carefully removed, and a tooth-matching resin material is bonded directly to the tooth.

Unlike older amalgam (silver) fillings, composite fillings blend seamlessly with the natural tooth colour, require less removal of healthy tooth structure, and bond directly to the tooth for added strength. They are safe, durable, and aesthetically natural-looking.

Early treatment of cavities with composite fillings prevents deeper decay, avoids root canal treatment, and saves the tooth long-term — all in a single visit.
Composite Filling Cavity Treatment Tooth Restoration Single Visit
Before

Composite Filling

Lower Molar Restoration — Cavity Treated with Tooth-Coloured Filling

Lower molars bear the greatest chewing load in the mouth, making them highly susceptible to cavities — especially in the grooves and pits of the biting surface. Early detection through regular check-ups allows treatment before the decay reaches the nerve.

In this case, the decayed portion of the lower molar was removed and restored with a tooth-coloured composite resin, matched precisely to the natural shade of the tooth. The result is a strong, fully functional, and completely natural-looking restoration.

Composite fillings on lower molars are completed in a single appointment — no temporary fillings, no second visit needed.
Composite Filling Molar Restoration Cavity Treatment Single Visit

Fixed Bridge

Missing Upper Front Teeth Restored with a Fixed Bridge

This patient presented with multiple missing upper front teeth, inflamed gums, and malaligned remaining teeth — significantly affecting appearance, confidence, and chewing ability.

A fixed dental bridge was fabricated to replace the missing teeth. Unlike removable dentures, a fixed bridge is cemented permanently onto the adjacent supporting teeth, providing a stable, natural-looking, and fully functional result. The patient's smile was completely transformed in a predictable, comfortable procedure.

A fixed bridge requires no removal for cleaning, feels like natural teeth, and restores full chewing function — making it one of the most comfortable tooth replacement options.
Fixed Dental Bridge Front Teeth Restoration Smile Makeover Teeth Replacement
Oral Surgery

Third Molar Disimpaction — Wisdom Tooth Removal Surgery

Impacted wisdom teeth (third molars) are one of the most common reasons for oral surgery. When a wisdom tooth does not have enough space to erupt fully, it becomes impacted — trapped beneath the gum or against the adjacent tooth — causing pain, swelling, infection, and damage to neighbouring teeth.

At Friendly Dental Care, disimpaction surgery is performed under local anaesthesia by Dr. Priti Shethna, assisted by a visiting Oral & Maxillofacial Surgeon, ensuring a safe, controlled, and comfortable procedure. The surgical site heals fully within 1–2 weeks with proper post-operative care.

Signs you may need wisdom tooth removal Pain at the back of the jaw, swollen or bleeding gums, difficulty opening the mouth, or recurring infections near the last molar.
Wisdom Tooth Removal Oral Surgery Local Anaesthesia 3rd Molar Disimpaction

Orthodontics

Orthodontic Correction — From Crowded Teeth to a Confident Smile

This patient presented with crowded and malaligned upper front teeth, affecting both aesthetics and bite function. Crowding occurs when there is insufficient space in the jaw for teeth to erupt in proper alignment — a very common condition that is highly treatable at any age.

Metal braces were fitted and adjusted over the course of treatment, progressively guiding each tooth into its ideal position. Once the desired alignment was achieved, a fixed bonded retainer wire was placed on the inner surface of the teeth to maintain the correction long-term — invisible from the outside and requiring no daily removal.

Retainers are essential after braces — teeth have a natural tendency to drift back without retention. A bonded retainer holds the result permanently without any effort from the patient.
Metal Braces Orthodontic Correction Bonded Retainer Teeth Alignment

Root Canal

Dental Abscess Resolved with Root Canal Treatment

This patient presented with a dental abscess — a painful bacterial infection at the root of the tooth causing localised swelling and pus accumulation at the gum line. Without treatment, the infection spreads rapidly to surrounding bone and tissue.

Root canal treatment (RCT) was performed to remove the infected pulp tissue, clean and shape the root canals, and seal the tooth to prevent reinfection. Following RCT, the abscess drained completely and the surrounding gum tissue healed, eliminating pain and saving the natural tooth.

Root canal treatment has a very high success rate and allows patients to keep their natural tooth for many years — often for life — with a crown placed on top for long-term protection.
Root Canal Treatment Abscess Drainage Pulp Infection Tooth Preservation

Tooth Extraction

Severely Decayed Molar — When Extraction is the Only Option

This patient presented with a severely decayed lower molar where the cavity had extended deep into the root, making the tooth unrestorable. When decay reaches this stage, neither a filling nor root canal treatment can adequately save the tooth — extraction becomes the only safe and appropriate option.

The extracted tooth clearly shows the extent of destruction — a large, dark cavity penetrating through the crown deep into the root structure, with the surrounding tissue showing signs of chronic infection. Early treatment at an earlier stage could have saved the tooth with a filling or root canal.

Don't wait until it's too late Regular check-ups catch decay early — when it can still be treated with a simple filling. Once decay reaches the root, the tooth cannot be saved.

Scaling & Polishing

Teeth Cleaning — Scaling & Polishing for Healthier Gums

These cases show heavy tartar (calculus) and stain buildup — including significant deposits on the lingual (tongue-side) surfaces visible through the dental mirror. Calculus accumulates from irregular brushing, tobacco use, or the natural tendency of some individuals to deposit minerals. It cannot be removed by brushing alone; it requires professional cleaning.

Scaling and polishing was performed using an ultrasonic scaler to remove all calculus deposits and surface stains, followed by polishing to smooth the tooth surfaces and make them more resistant to future plaque accumulation. The result — cleaner teeth, fresher breath, and healthier gums.

Professional scaling every 6 months prevents gum disease (gingivitis and periodontitis), reduces bad breath, and keeps your teeth looking their best. It is one of the most important preventive dental treatments available.
Scaling & Polishing Tartar Removal Gum Disease Prevention Preventive Dentistry

Fixed Bridge

Lower Front Teeth Restored with a Full Fixed Bridge

This patient presented with severely decayed and discoloured lower anterior teeth — heavily stained, structurally compromised, and causing significant aesthetic and functional concerns. The remaining tooth structure was insufficient for individual crowns, making a full fixed bridge the ideal solution.

Following extraction of the non-restorable teeth and preparation of the supporting abutment teeth, a full-arch fixed ceramic bridge was fabricated and cemented. The result is a complete transformation — natural-looking, well-aligned lower teeth that restore the patient's smile, chewing function, and confidence in a single fixed solution.

A fixed bridge is permanently cemented and functions exactly like natural teeth — no removal, no adhesives, no compromise. Patients typically adapt within days and forget they have a bridge at all.
Fixed Dental Bridge Full Arch Restoration Ceramic Crown Smile Transformation

Dental Crowns

Fractured Front Teeth Restored with Dental Crowns

This young patient sustained fractures to multiple upper front teeth — a common result of sports injuries, falls, or accidents. The jagged, uneven edges affected both appearance and function, causing self-consciousness and difficulty biting.

Dental crowns were fabricated and placed over the fractured teeth, completely restoring their shape, size, and strength. The result is a natural-looking, confident smile — fully functional and protected from further damage. Crowns are one of the most durable and aesthetic solutions for fractured or severely damaged front teeth.

Fractured front teeth should be treated promptly — exposed dentine causes sensitivity and is vulnerable to decay. Crowns provide full coverage protection and can last 10–15 years with proper care.
Dental Crowns Front Teeth Restoration Tooth Fracture Smile Makeover

Root Extraction

Decayed Root Stumps — Multiple Root Piece Extractions

This patient presented with multiple severely decayed lower teeth reduced to root stumps — the crown portions had been destroyed by long-standing, untreated decay. Six root pieces were carefully extracted under local anaesthesia in a single surgical session.

Retained root pieces that are left in the jaw can cause chronic infection, pain, cyst formation, and bone loss over time. Timely removal clears the infection, allows the bone to heal, and prepares the site for future teeth replacement — such as dentures, bridges, or implants.

Retained roots are not harmless Even painless root stumps harbour bacteria, cause hidden bone loss, and can develop into cysts. Removal is always recommended — the sooner, the simpler the procedure.
Root Piece Extraction Surgical Extraction Multiple Extractions Bone Preservation

Patient education & awareness

Know your dental health.

Understanding your oral health helps you make better decisions and prevent problems before they start.

5 Benefits of Dental Crowns

Dental crowns are one of the most versatile restorations in dentistry. They protect damaged teeth, restore full chewing function, improve appearance, and prevent further decay — all in one solution.

Does not decay Protects from damage Restores function Improves appearance

Correct Toothpaste Amount for Children

Many parents use too much toothpaste for their children. For kids under 3, use a grain-of-rice sized smear. For ages 3–6, a pea-sized amount is sufficient. Excess fluoride from swallowed toothpaste can cause dental fluorosis.

Paediatric Dental Tip Fluoride Safety Oral Hygiene

Common Causes of Sensitive Teeth

Tooth sensitivity is often a sign of an underlying issue. Causes include enamel erosion, gum recession, tooth grinding, deep decay, and over-brushing. Identifying the cause is the first step to effective treatment.

Enamel Erosion Gum Recession Grinding / Clenching Decay

Free Dental Screening Camp

At Friendly Dental Care, we believe preventive care starts with awareness. Dr. Priti Shethna regularly conducts free dental screening camps — examining patients of all ages, identifying problems early, and guiding families on oral hygiene. Early detection saves teeth and prevents costly treatment later.

Community Outreach Free Screening Preventive Care All Ages Welcome

Proper Brushing Technique

Most people brush too hard, too fast, or at the wrong angle. The correct technique: hold your brush at 45° to the gumline, use gentle circular motions on outer surfaces, sweep up-and-down on inner surfaces, brush your tongue, floss between teeth, and finish with mouthwash. Brush for at least 2 minutes, twice a day.

45° Angle Circular Motion Floss Daily 2 Minutes Twice Daily
